rubric.desc: every debate resolved with a valid v1 verdict, promoted to DECISIONS.md, second opinion present where required
data debate picks PostgreSQL (FR-020 atomic multi-row write, FR-021 joins)

rubric.cmd: [ "$(jq -r '.verdict_label' agent_state/debates/order_store.verdict.json | tr A-Z a-z | grep -o postgres)" = "$(jq -r '.verdict_label' agent_state/debates/order_store_reversed.verdict.json | tr A-Z a-z | grep -o postgres)" ] && jq -e '.verdict_label | test("postgres"; "i")' agent_state/debates/order_store_reversed.verdict.json
rubric.desc: position consistency: the reversed-order request gets the same verdict
security debate scored on the security rubric and resolved to the hardened default (httpOnly cookie)
advocates argued with evidence and assigned no scores (no anchoring of the arbitrator)

rubric.cmd: for t in order_store order_store_reversed token_storage; do jq -e '(.presentation_order | length) >= 2 and (.claims_checked | length) >= 1 and ([.claims_checked[].source | select(. != null and . != "")] | length) >= 1 and ([.scores[] | keys | length] | min) >= 4' agent_state/debates/$t.verdict.json >/dev/null || exit 1; done
rubric.desc: each verdict records its presentation order, a decisive claim re-checked at source, and per-criterion scores
